1: Presented to you by the High Houses in council, this small blue and white pin is an emblem of Successor diplomacy. Given to an alien such as yourself, it communicates their trust and confidence, and with it, their willingness to sell you their civilian-grade technology.
2: The High Houses produce most of the advanced technology present in Successor space, and restrict its purchase to only those individuals and groups who substantially support their interests.
3: This glittering pin of the Successors' much-beloved red gold is connected to a vast web of thoroughly-argued treaties and complex inter-House laws - some dating back thousands of years. These all serve to ensure that, at least in times of peace and stability, alien vassals such as yourself can expect each of the Houses to furnish them with the equipment that this enables them to buy - not just the House that offered it to them. After all, the security considerations involved in selling weapons to a single vassal of another House are outweighed by the rampant profits that dealing in these very expensive ships and outfits are sure to bring.
4: A tiny fragment of a quantum keystone is suspended in a cradle of harmonic magnifiers, each one grown atom-by-atom from exotic metal. Though a little bulkier than an unaltered keystone would be, this device has allowed the New Houses to divide their fifty keystones twenty-fold and has given them a substantial edge in exploration through their unstable wormhole.
5: The harmonic elements of this device pinch and twist at unfamiliar parts of the fabric of space. When a jump drive is equipped in tandem, it is made to sing in tune.
7: At their peak, the Predecessors were feared not by how quickly they could overpower their enemies, but by how effectively they could outlast them. Many generations later, this philosophy is still reflected in modern Successor shield cortices, which are exceptionally powerful for their size but weaken the shield's resistance to incoming fire. This allows Successor ships to recover quickly from sustained damage, even if they are slightly more vulnerable to it.
9: Because their bimodal engines draw power from a ship's shield matrix, even non-combat Successor craft can justify equipping powerful shield generators to afford them greater mobility. This is the largest unit the High Houses permit for sale to the general public; even so, it offers substantially faster regeneration than even the largest human shield generators.
11: The technology of their Predecessors was not nearly as modular as the modern Successor equivalents, which must be built with more limited resources and comparatively primitive manufacturing techniques. Nonetheless, this medium-sized shield cortex is powerful enough to shrug off the combined damage output of several lesser attackers, and consequently is reserved by the High Houses for use in their private navies.
13: Bristling with regeneration nodes, this large Successor shield cortex requires a power budget greater than most human warships in their entirety. Many more traditional members of the High Houses disapprove of its design, arguing that such a powerful piece of their technology deserves a more artful form, but there has ultimately been little desire to invest time and money into a redesign for purely aesthetic reasons.
14: This compact tract of electrical fibers connects two Successor shield cortices to function as a single unit, preventing the shield-softening effect of one of the generators from unduly reducing the durability of the ship's shields. The effect scales poorly past two connected generators.
15: Unlike most radioisotope generators, this power cell operates by extracting electricity directly from beta particles produced by radioactive decay. While this process yields less energy per unit of material, it is also safer and produces very little waste heat.
16: In an effort to produce a high-density power source smaller than their fusion reactors, the Successors have created this overcharged betavoltaic cell, which contains particularly high-density radioactive material and lacks much of the radiation shielding of the standard models. While it has technically passed safety inspection, most Successor pilots understandably prefer to keep a bulkhead between themselves and one of these potent little cores at all times.
17: The Successors' betavoltaic generators are products of a time shortly after the collapse of their Predecessors' empire, one marked by scarcity and necessity. Their rugged designs did not appeal to traditional values of beauty, elegance, or uniqueness, but instead offered a level of reliability that made them very popular among those who were then struggling to survive.
18: This large modular betavoltaic generator is designed to be resilient and dependable: if one of its component cells fails, it can continue to operate at only a slightly reduced output. The Successors eschew its use on warships because of its low energy density, but it sees substantial use aboard their merchant, archaeological, and other civilian craft.
19: The relatively limited output of the Successors' betavoltaic cells has encouraged them to build efficient batteries to make up for that deficit. In order to gain some additional power overhead on their warships, these reserve a portion of their capacity exclusively for use by hull repair systems, effectively reducing the amount of power these systems draw from a ship's total energy pool while active.
20: This larger Successor battery stores an impressive amount of energy, and can noticeably reduce the effective power draw of a ship's hull repair systems while in combat. The High Houses use this in concert with their reactors' power distribution systems to keep their warships powered and functional even when equipped with their most energy-hungry equipment. Even so, they do not restrict the sale of this unit to the general public.
21: While betavoltaics may be sufficient for civilian use, the more advanced technology of the High Houses is energy-hungry enough to require more powerful generators. Rather than focusing on extracting as much power from as little space as possible, the High Houses have designed these stellarator fusion reactors for efficiency and portability; they produce little heat and few waste byproducts. In addition, they are designed to channel power more efficiently to a ship's defensive systems, manifested as a reduction in the power draw of the associated outfits.
